solid
label: Solid
description: Which of the five Platonic solids. Each one has its own classic net: the choice changes the whole net, its creases and its glue seams.

name: edge_length
label: Edge length
description: Length of one edge of the solid. The largest edge is the one whose net with its tabs still fits your sheet inside the margins.

name: fold_percent
label: Fold it shut
description: Drag from 0 (the flat net) to 100 (the closed solid). Every crease folds together.

name: sheet
label: Sheet of paper
description: The sheet your printer takes. The pattern goes along its long side, so print landscape; the edge length is limited so the pattern fits.

name: paper_weight
label: Paper weight (g/m2)
description: The paper's weight as printed on the pack (80 office paper, 160 thin card, 250 card). It sets the paper's thickness, which sets back each tab's corners by one paper thickness, and the mass.

name: tab_depth
label: Glue tab width
description: How far a glue tab sticks out from the edge it glues: at most a quarter of the edge length, and no wider than the sheet still has room for. Every seam has one tab.

title: Platonic net to fold and glue
author: 3DCraft Jigs
description: Each of the five Platonic solids from one sheet of paper. Pick a solid, set its size for your sheet and drag Fold it shut to watch the classic net close. To print it, use File > Export and choose Crease pattern of [solid] print pattern, as SVG or DXF. Print at 100 % and in landscape: the file is only as big as the pattern, so portrait cuts part of it off. Cut on the solid outline, fold away from you on the dash-dot lines (faces and tabs alike) and glue each tab under the edge it meets. The plain net without tabs is Crease pattern of [solid] net.
